text:
alex: Quick Q — running into weirdness with the CLI when I combine profiles + env vars in CI. Which wins exactly? I set RW_PROFILE=staging but also have credentials in ~/.redwood/cli/profiles.yaml for 'staging' and a RW_API_KEY in the env. Sometimes the CLI picks the file creds, sometimes the env key. Anyone seen this?

maria: env should override file by design, but there was a bug in 1.3.1 where profile-level keys were preferred during streaming calls. can you paste the exact command you run?

alex: i do `rwd-cli chat --model redwood-v1 --profile staging` inside a docker container, and the container has RW_API_KEY set via GitHub Actions secrets. local config file still has an older token. sometimes the request fails with 401 then next attempt succeeds.

jordan: that 401 -> 200 smell is the old merge-order race. confirm your CLI version: `rwd-cli --version`. deploy-bot pushed a fix in 1.3.2 that flips merge precedence to env -> profile -> global.

alex: `rwd-cli --version` shows `1.3.1` 🤦‍♂️. ok will upgrade.

deploy-bot: heads-up: release 1.3.2 rolled out 2026-02-12. change-log: "env vars now consistently override profile values; streaming progress no longer resets merge context". Upgrade recommended. :rocket:

maria: also: if you're piping streaming output to tools like `jq` or `sed`, the CLI's progress spinner can break chunked output. either use `--no-progress` or set `TERM=dumb` in CI. example: `TERM=dumb rwd-cli chat --stream --no-progress | jq -r .text`

alex: ahhh that explains my pipe truncation. i was seeing partial json chunks. thanks.

sam: fyi for retries in CI scripts we use a tiny wrapper that retries non-5xx errors only for auth hiccups. snippet we use:```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
retries=5
backoff=1
for i in $(seq 1 $retries); do
  if rwd-cli some-command --profile "$RW_PROFILE"; then
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep $backoff
  backoff=$((backoff * 2))
done
exit 1
```

sam: this keeps transient 401s from flapping pipelines while we roll upgrades. also check that the container doesn't have an older binary cached.

jordan: one more gotcha: macOS keychain integration writes tokens to `~/Library/Keychains/__redwood_token` and the CLI will read that unless `RW_NO_KEYCHAIN=1` is set. if your CI runner is macos-hosted, that could explain fallback to file creds.

alex: thanks all — plan: upgrade CLI to 1.3.2, add `--no-progress` to stream commands in CI, and wrap calls with the retry script. i'll also `export RW_NO_KEYCHAIN=1` in our job to force env-first behavior while we roll. i'll post back if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

maria: sounds good. ping me if you want me to open an infra PR to update the GitHub Actions runner images.

alex: will do. thanks!
